target_customer: University and high school students in Denmark, Sweden, Germany and beyond who pay for exam prep
problem: Students have generic course materials and need personalized study tools and exam practice tied to their own slides, notes and past exams.
business_model: Consumer freemium subscription per Business Insider
product_category: AI exam prep and personalized learning

founders.name: Kim Rants
education: Imperial College London, MSc Computer Science
London School of Economics, MSc Finance
founders.background_notes: More than 10 years teaching university students per YC page.

founders.name: Patrick Gadd
education: University of Oxford, MSc Computer Science
founders.background_notes: YC page gives only the first name; surname from Seedtable coverage.

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating quizzes, flashcards, podcasts and chat grounded in uploaded material with source page citations uses available LLM tooling, with reliability on personal course content the main work.

defensibility.rationale: Many AI study apps offer the same features and features are copyable in weeks. Distribution and student habits are the only edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established. General LLM assistants added study modes during 2025 but no source ties them to Alice.

market_need_then: Students widely adopted AI for studying, and the YC page reports $20k MRR growing about 10% weekly for 8 weeks at the time of the Winter 2025 batch.

identity.voice_and_tone: friendly, positioned as Duolingo for exams

branding.community_and_virality: Company claims 100,000+ students on its site, while other sources cite 2,000, 10,000 or 250,000, so usage claims are inconsistent.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly human name with a clear comparison line, but the name is shared by many unrelated companies and no brand specific press was found.

outcome_analysis: Alice.tech raised a seed in May 2025 led by Cherry Ventures with Y Combinator and PSV Tech, after a Winter 2025 batch with reported $20k MRR growing quickly. The CEO has a decade of university teaching experience, matching the product. The study tool space is crowded and easy to copy, and its total funding is reported near $5.6M to $6M, so later outcomes remain open with no shutdown or acquisition reported.
notes: Amount conflict: $4.8M (Business Insider and most outlets) versus 4.2 million euros (EU-Startups syndicates) and $4.2M or $4.7M in databases. The pre-seed led by PSV has no date or amount found. A Cherry Ventures job listing and the company about page say about $5.6M to over $6M raised in total. No dated competitor sources near the Winter 2025 batch were found; Prismara (June 2025) and others are after the batch, so the list is empty.
